headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty extended their losing streak to an eighth consecutive week amid heavy foreign institutional selling.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Heavy selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) dragged benchmark indices down.
Surging global crude oil prices and global rate hike concerns fueled persistent capital outflows.
Elevated global geopolitical and economic risks continued to weigh on investor sentiment.
Broad-based market selling marked the longest weekly losing streak for Indian equities in 25 years.
whatHappening: Indian stock markets are closed today, October 2, 2026, on account of Gandhi Jayanti.
On the last trading day, Sensex dropped 570.59 points while Nifty closed down at 22,421.95.
Indian benchmark indices posted an eighth consecutive weekly decline, with Nifty50 and Sensex falling up to 3% over the week.
Shyam Metalics announced a deal to invest over $5 billion in Maharashtra.
summary: Indian markets are closed today for the Gandhi Jayanti holiday and will reopen on Monday, October 5. In the last trading session, Sensex fell 570.59 points to mark the eighth consecutive week of losses due to en-masse FII selling. Key corporate actions include Shyam Metalics committing over $5 billion in Maharashtra investments.
